Every pod serves a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at `/mcp`, for example `https://pod.example.com/mcp`. AI
clients use it to read your pod and to propose changes to it, under the permissions of their key.

Most people never configure it by hand: `synap connect <client>` writes the client's MCP configuration. See
[Connect an agent](/docs/build/agents).

## Transport

MCP Streamable HTTP:

| Request | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /mcp` | A JSON-RPC 2.0 request. The answer is JSON or an SSE stream. |
| `GET /mcp` | An SSE stream for messages the server initiates. |
| `DELETE /mcp` | Ends the session. |

The server negotiates the protocol version with the client; it is not pinned to one revision.

## Authentication

Send a key as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

- A request without a valid key gets `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…"` header pointing at
  the pod's OAuth metadata (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`). Clients such as claude.ai use it to sign in
  through the pod's own OAuth server and obtain a key, with no key to paste.
- Too many requests get `429`.

## Scopes

The tools a key can call depend on its scopes:

| Key scope | MCP access |
|---|---|
| `mcp.read`, `hub-protocol.read` or `data.read` | read tools |
| `mcp.write`, `hub-protocol.write` or `data.write` | read and write tools |
| `hub-protocol.admin` | read and write tools |

A key with none of these can call no tool. A key whose grant is narrower than full access can read only through the
tools whose reads its grant bounds; other read tools answer `GRANT_DOOR_UNSUPPORTED`. See
[API keys](/docs/build/api-keys#doors-a-scoped-key-can-read-through).

## Governance

Every write tool goes through the same permission check as any other write to the pod: the change is applied only
where a rule allows it, and otherwise becomes a proposal that a person approves. No MCP tool can approve a proposal
with an agent's key.

## Tools

All tool names start with `synap_`, for example `synap_ask` to ask the pod a question in natural language. A new
agent key lists a small entry set of tools and loads the others in groups. [MCP tools](/docs/reference/mcp-tools)
lists every tool with its parameters, generated from the backend's tool definitions.

## Test the endpoint

```bash
synap mcp verify
```

checks that `/mcp` answers and that your key is valid.
